_comment: Player identity rules for the historic import.
Identity is resolved primarily by chess.com username, which is stable and
unambiguous. Display names are NOT reliable on their own: two different
people both appear as 'Kyle', and several people are recorded under a
shortened or lengthened name in different seasons.
The importer unions entries that share a username, then applies the
explicit rules below. Anything it cannot resolve is a hard error, never a
silent guess.
username -> the display name to store. Where a person appears under
several names across seasons, the most recent one wins.
ASSUMPTION, FLAGGED FOR REVIEW. These are one person who changed their
chess.com username between seasons, merged on the strength of an
identical display name plus never appearing in the same tournament.
If either is actually two different people, split them here.
The value is the username to keep (the later one).
Different people who share a first name. Listed so a future maintainer
does not 'helpfully' merge them.
historic username -> the spelling already in the live players table.
Applied last, after username_changes, so historic results attach to the
existing live player rather than creating a duplicate.
Michael: tournaments 12 and 14 both print 'KnotYourCapitan' (cap-i-tan);
the live database has 'knotyourcaptain' (cap-tain). Confirmed by cropping
and upscaling tournament-14/standings.jpeg. Decision: the live spelling is
the real chess.com account and the source sheets carry the typo, so the
live spelling wins and the chess.com game lookup keeps working.
Historic people who must NOT be merged into a same-named live player.
The importer creates a second row for these on purpose.

Andy.reason: Decision: treated as two different people despite the shared display name. Both rows will read 'Andy'; the chess.com username is what tells them apart, and the admin player dropdown shows it.

not_players._comment: Placeholder rows in standings tables. Dropped, never imported.

_comment: scripts/seed-players.mjs and the live players table list Andy as
'randongles'. Three independent historic sources (tournament 1 Group B,
tournament 4 A Division, and the tournament 14 standings image) all say
'randiddly'. Decision: these are two different people, so the live row is
left untouched and the historic Andy is imported as a separate player.
See deliberately_separate_from_live above.
